他非常自以爲是——就像是一生都沒做過錯事似的。

NONE: › flour containing a substance that makes cakes swell when they are cooked
自發麵粉
› the act of a country, a part of a country, or a nation choosing its own government and controlling its own activities
自治

example: See also

NONE: › giving up what you want so that other people can have what they want
自我犧牲

example: People say this is a selfish society, but frankly I've seen too much kindness, self-sacrifice and generosity to believe that.
人們說這是個自私的社會，但坦白地說，我看過太多善良、自我犧牲和慷慨之舉，因此不會輕信這個說法。
The job requires a lot of enthusiasm, dedication and self-sacrifice.
這項工作需要極大的熱情、奉獻和自我犧牲的精神。

NONE: › very pleased with yourself and showing no criticism of yourself
自滿的；自鳴得意的

example: She was very smug and self-satisfied about getting the promotion.
她爲升職而很是沾沾自喜，神氣活現。

NONE: › interested in your own advantage in everything that you do
圖謀私利的

example: A lot of people feel that politicians are just self-seeking opportunists.
很多人覺得掌權的政客僅僅是圖私利的機會主義分子。

NONE: › involving people or organizations that choose to take part in an activity, rather than being chosen by someone else
自我選拔的

example: a self-selected sample of boys
一群自我選拔的男孩樣本

NONE: B1 especially in a shop or restaurant, not being served by an employee but collecting goods or food yourself
（尤指商店或餐廳）自選的，自助的

example: a self-service salad bar
自助沙拉吧

NONE: › working or acting for your own advantage
追逐私利的

example: Politicians are seen as corrupt and self-serving.
政客被視爲追逐私利的腐敗分子。

NONE: › a person who is able to work effectively without regularly needing to be told what to do
有主動性的人；工作主動的人

example: The successful applicant for the position will be a well-motivated self-starter who has excellent communication skills.
能獲得這個職位的應徵者必須具有出色的溝通技巧，工作積極主動。

NONE: › a way of learning about a subject that involves studying alone at home, rather than in a classroom with a teacher
自學

example: The diploma is awarded following a course of self-study ending in a three-hour exam.
在完成自學課程和3小時考試之後將獲得證書。

NONE: › given a name or title by yourself without any official reason for it
自封的；自稱的

媒體上似乎滿是自封的「專家」，他們樂於對自己實際上知之甚少的話題發表見解。

NONE: C2 able to provide everything you need, especially food, for yourself without the help of other people
（尤指食物）自給自足的

example: The programme aims to make the country self-sufficient in food production and to cut energy imports.
這個企劃案旨在使國家在糧食上能自給自足，並減少能源進口。

NONE: › earning or having enough money to pay for your activities without receiving financial help from other people
自給的；自立的

example: The vast majority of students here are self-supporting.
這裡的絕大多數學生都是自己負擔學費。

self-financing

NONE: › a substance that you put on your skin to make it look darker as if you have been in the sun
仿曬乳（塗於皮膚上的一種物質，使皮膚看起來黝黑，好像被太陽曬過一樣）
› Someone who is self-taught has taught himself or herself a particular skill.
自己學會的

example: a self-taught musician/furniture maker/cook
自學成材的樂師／傢俱製作者／廚師
Most of these artists are self-taught.
這些藝術家絕大部分是自學成材的。

NONE: › determined to base your actions on your own decisions without listening to advice from other people
固執的，任性的
› the value you give to your life and achievements
自我價值

example: Many people derive their self-worth from their work.
很多人從自己的工作中找到自身的價值。

NONE: › informal a photograph that you take of yourself , usually with a mobile phone. Selfies are often published using social media.
自拍照

example: He posted a series of close-up selfies on his Instagram yesterday.
他在自己的Instagram網頁上登出了一系列自拍照。

NONE: › a long device that you can attach to your mobile phone and use for taking a selfie (= a photograph of yourself) from a distance, so you can fit more people or things into the picture
自拍照杆
B1 Someone who is selfish only thinks of their own advantage
自私的

example: The judge told him: "Your attitude shows a selfish disregard for others."
法官告訴他：「你的態度表明你只顧自己而不顧他人。」

NONE: › caring more for what other people need and want rather than for what you yourself need and want
無私的
› exactly the same
完全相同的，同一的

example: His father had suffered from the selfsame disease.
他的父親曾得過同樣的病。

I or T: A2 [ I or T ] to give something to someone else in return for money
A2 [ I or T ] to be bought in the way or quantities that are mentioned; to be sold at the price mentioned
被以（…方式／數量／價格）購買

T: C2 [ T ] to persuade someone that an idea or plan is a good one and likely to be successful

example: We'll be selling the tickets at/for £50 each.
我們每張票將賣50英鎊。
The stall sells drinks and snacks.
這個攤位賣飲料和小吃。
These baskets sell well (= a lot of them are bought).
這些籃子賣得很好。
Their last album sold over a hundred thousand copies.
他們的最新唱片賣出了超過10萬張。
How much does the phone sell for?
這部電話賣多少錢？
My boss is very old-fashioned and I'm having a lot of trouble selling the idea of working at home occasionally.
我的上司很守舊，我要費好大的功夫才能使他相信偶爾在家裡工作是個不錯的主意。
The filmmakers sold me on the idea that my book would work on the screen.
這位電影人士說服了我，讓我相信我的小說可以搬上銀幕。
[ + two objects ] The chance of greater access to European markets would help sell the president the plan/sell the plan to the president.
有機會更進一步打入歐洲市場將能說服總統接受這個計劃。
In an interview, you have to sell yourself to the employer.
在面試時，你必須想辦法打動雇主。

NONE: › to not do what you have promised someone you will do or what you should do because you will get more advantages for yourself if you do something else
背叛；出賣

example: French farmers feel they've been sold out by their government in the negotiations.
法國農民感到在談判中他們被政府出賣了。
They've sold out to the oil lobby (= done what these people wanted).
他們讓自己被石油行業遊說團收買了。

NONE: › to sell all of the supply that you have of something
賣光
B2 If a supply of something sells out, there is no more of that thing to buy.
銷售一空，售罄；脫售

passive: › [ passive ] When a film, concert, etc. is sold out, all of the tickets for it have been sold.

NONE: › to sell your business or part of your business
出售（部分）企業

我們在前幾個小時就把T恤賣完了。
The first issue of the magazine sold out within two days.
雜誌的第一期兩天內銷售一空。

我們弄不到座位——音樂會的票賣完了。
They decided to sell out to their competitors.
他們決定把公司賣給競爭對手。

NONE: › to deceive someone into buying or believing something that has no value
誆騙（某人）購買毫無價值的東西
› to put someone in a difficult or dangerous situation by not acting as you had promised to act, usually in order to win an advantage for yourself
出賣（某人）；背叛（某人）
› to not consider someone or something to be as valuable or good as he, she, or it deserves
小看；低估

example: Don't sell yourself short - you've got the skills and the experience.
不要小看自己——你有技術，也有經驗。

NONE: › to charge a low price for something to encourage people to buy it
減價出售；低價處理
› to sell all or part of a business
出售（全部或部分企業）

example: They're selling off last year's stock at half price.
他們正以半價拋售去年的存貨。
The company announced that it would be selling off its hotel business.
公司宣佈將出售其旅館業務。

NONE: › to sell your house or company in order to go somewhere else or do something else
（爲移居他處或做別的事情而）出售房屋（或公司）

example: They sold up and retired to the West Country.
他們變賣家產搬到了英格蘭西南部。

NONE: › to be persuaded to do something, especially something bad, because of the money or other reward you will receive for doing it
出賣靈魂

（商品上標明的）到期日，保存期限
› a sale of an unwanted business at a low price to encourage someone to buy it
低價出售；廉價處理

（股票等的）拋售

（商店或工廠內的貨物）廉價拋售

example: Compare

NONE: B1 a person who is selling something
賣方，銷售者

暢銷商品

賣花／賣報／賣紀念品的人

你覺得房屋賣主會接受30萬歐元的價格嗎？
This car is our biggest seller so far this year.
這種汽車是我們目前賣得最好的一款。

NONE: › a characteristic of a product that will persuade people to buy it
賣點

example: Its best selling point is the price - it's the cheapest on the market.
其最大賣點在於價格——這是市場上最便宜的。

NONE: › a brand name for a long, thin strip of sticky and usually transparent material that is sold in a roll and is used for joining together things such as paper or card
（賽勒塔普）透明膠帶

example: a roll of Sellotape
一捲透明膠帶
I stuck the note to the door with Sellotape.
我用透明膠帶把便條貼在門上。

Scotch tape

C usually singular: › a performance or sports event for which no more tickets are available, because it is so popular
票全部售出的演出（或比賽）；滿座的演出（或比賽）
› disapproving a situation in which someone does not do what they have promised to do or what they should do
